clue.text: Rashness gets us right in front

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for right is put inside the word for front

parts.note: front is brazen cheek, i.e. impudence

explanation.surface: Someone complains that recklessness lets us push straight to the front of a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside IMPUDENCE; 'front' here is the noun meaning nerve or cheek, not a position.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence is a lack of caution, so it is a synonym for rashness.

clue.text: Part of trail exhibiting common holly

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a nature trail shows off the everyday holly bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus name of holly, used for the common holly itself.

clue.text: As cover for joint, left a special — plate on

indicators.note: on says the next pieces are placed after the rearranged plate
special is read as specially arranged, so the letters of plate are reworked

explanation.surface: A diner is told a special plate will cover the joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' looks like a description of the plate on a menu but is the anagram signal; 'on' attaches the abbreviation and the article; the joint is the knee, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is a bone that covers and protects the knee joint, so it acts as cover for a joint.

clue.text: Writer is in nude resort? .'It's not sanctioned

indicators.note: in puts the writer and is inside the jumbled letters
resort is read as re-sort, sorting the letters of nude again

parts.note: a writer is an author
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novelist turns up at a naturist resort, which is frowned upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place (a naturist resort) but is read as re-sort, the anagram signal; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Unauthorised describes something done without official permission, i.e. not sanctioned.

clue.text: Endlessly bespangled like Black Beauty

indicators.note: Endlessly says the word loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: bespangled means covered in sequins, sequined

explanation.surface: A glittering costume makes someone look endlessly like a famous horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' strips S and D from SEQUINED. Black Beauty is the horse in Anna Sewell's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine means relating to or resembling horses, and Black Beauty is a fictional horse.

clue.text: The broadsword is mine, sort of

definitions.meaning: a kind of directional anti-personnel mine bears the same name

explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' is not the possessive pronoun but an explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Highland broadsword and to a type of military mine.

clue.text: Enter with this fish to get chips

definitions.text: Enter with this fish to get chips

parts.words: Enter with this fish to get chips
parts.note: put the fish's name before the word enter and you get a tradesman whose nickname is Chips

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' is a traditional British nickname for a carpenter, from wood chips; it is not fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish is a freshwater species which, joined to the word enter, makes the woodworker called Chips.

clue.text: Stake a girl put up, one feels

parts.note: a stake in poker is the ante

indicators.note: put up, in a down clue, means the girl's name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a girl's claim by putting up a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ANN into NNA beneath ANTE; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an insect's feeler, so it is something that feels.

clue.text: Promotion put pressure on soldiers to crush unrest

indicators.note: on says the soldiers follow the pressure

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
ferment is agitation or unrest

explanation.surface: An officer's promotion came after he leaned on troops to put down a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' and 'to crush' only join the pieces; RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Preferment is advancement to a higher office, which is a synonym for promotion.

clue.text: Vehicle once seen by Russian river, outside city walls

parts.note: ex means former, once
a tram is a vehicle
the Ural is a river in Russia

explanation.surface: An old streetcar is spotted beside a river in Russia, beyond the town ramparts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle once' is EX-TRAM, a former tram; 'seen by' just joins it to URAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Extramural literally means outside the walls, from Latin extra muros, so outside city walls.

clue.text: Tamworth residence said to be an eyesore?

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken and a different spelling is entered

parts.note: a Tamworth is a British breed of pig, and a pig lives in a sty

explanation.surface: A pig's home is described as a blot on the landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tamworth is a ginger British pig breed, not the town. 'an eyesore' reads as an ugly sight but means a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Instrument REME lot create without a blunder

indicators.note: blunder is read as a verb telling the letters to go astray

parts.note: these words supply the anagram fodder; REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers

explanation.surface: Army engineers create an instrument without making a single mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' says the letters of REME LOT CREATE, less one A, are rearranged by 'blunder'.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrometer is a measuring instrument for electric charge or potential difference.

clue.text: There's something noble about the colour of her hair

definitions.text: There's something noble about the colour of her hair

parts.words: There's something noble about the colour of her hair
parts.note: noble suggests a noble metal, and the hair is the pale silvery shade named after that precious metal

explanation.walkthrough: 'noble' looks like aristocratic bearing, but chemists call unreactive precious metals noble.
explanation.definitionFit: This very pale silver-blonde hair colour takes its name from a noble metal.

clue.text: Impression little Tom produced with engraving

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of an English folk tale
a print is an impression taken from an engraving

explanation.surface: A small boy's portrait is produced from an engraved plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced with' only joins the pieces; Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of English folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbprint is the impression left by the pad of the thumb.

clue.text: Tricked European involved in direct confrontation

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up in, so the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: to have someone on is to trick them, so tricked is had on

explanation.surface: A European conned into a heated face-to-face dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' puts E inside HAD ON, the colloquial phrase for tricked.
explanation.definitionFit: Head-on means meeting face to face, directly, so it fits in direct confrontation.

clue.text: Image promoter's right to, shout from the housetops

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer, who promotes an image
a claim is a right to something

explanation.surface: A publicist insists on the right to announce something loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO is a public relations officer; the 's is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly, the idiom being to shout it from the housetops.

clue.text: See stock farmer corner a horse for breaking

indicators.note: for breaking says the letters are smashed and rearranged, as a horse is broken in

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram
taken as written
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A rancher traps a wild horse in a corner to break it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for breaking' shuffles CORNER, A and H; H is heroin, whose slang name is horse. 'See' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranchero is a Spanish-American rancher who raises cattle, so a stock farmer.

clue.text: Song mother goes over, first of all, in Girl Crazy?

indicators.note: goes over, in an across clue, means the mother word turns backwards

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the jumbled girl
Crazy means the letters of girl are scrambled
first of picks only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Mum flips over a girl song in the musical Girl Crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl Crazy' looks like the Gershwin musical title, but 'Crazy' is the anagram signal; 'goes over' reverses the mother, 'first of' picks a letter, and 'in' inserts it.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is an unaccompanied part-song of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Famous countertenor going about with resident

indicators.note: going about means the singer's name surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: Alfred Deller was a celebrated English countertenor

explanation.surface: A celebrated high-voiced singer travels around with a local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' puts W inside DELLER; Alfred Deller revived the countertenor voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller is one who lives in a place, i.e. a resident.

clue.text: Short, unpleasant interval for sea god

indicators.note: Short says the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: the tritone is the dissonant musical interval of three whole tones

explanation.surface: A brief nasty break in proceedings for a god of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' removes the E from TRITONE; 'interval' is musical, not a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Triton is the Greek sea god, son of Poseidon, who blows a conch shell.

clue.text: In Paris so much drink leads to : petulant outburst

parts.note: tant is French for so much
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: Drinking so much in Paris ends in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: TANT is French for so much.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is a fit of bad temper, which is a petulant outburst.

clue.text: Big cat about' to upset cosmetic liquid

indicators.note: about means the cat's name goes round the other word

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, means the little word is turned upside down

explanation.surface: A lion is about to knock over a bottle of skin cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like a phrase meaning on the point of, but 'about' is the container signal and 'upset' reverses the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a liquid preparation applied to the skin as a cosmetic.

clue.text: Wits are required to display such alertness in crisis

definitions.text: Wits are required to display such alertness in crisis

parts.words: Wits are required to display such alertness in crisis
parts.note: keeping your wits about you in an emergency is the quality of a calm, quick-thinking mind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wits' reads as clever people, but it means mental faculties.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means the ability to think and act calmly and quickly in an emergency.

clue.text: Head missing from French sculptor's Norse god

indicators.note: Head missing from says the first letter is removed

parts.note: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker

explanation.surface: A statue of a Scandinavian deity by a French sculptor has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head missing from' removes R from RODIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, is mostly shown the way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: shown the way means led

explanation.surface: A man is mostly guided along his path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, not a person; 'mostly' cuts LED to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island, hence the perhaps.

clue.text: Sunk in, as post may be

definitions.meaning: said of a fact that has been taken in and understood
mail sent by a recorded, insured delivery service

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunk in' is the idiom for something finally being understood.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both noticed and understood, and describes mail sent with recorded delivery.

clue.text: People of fashion accepting rupees for rent

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: the ton is an old term for fashionable society

explanation.surface: Fashionable society takes rupees as payment for lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment for housing, but it is the past participle of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the old past participle of rend, meaning ripped or torn.

clue.text: Rustic types going after Romans in play

parts.note: in Julius Caesar, Mark Antony's speech begins Friends, Romans, followed by a third word

explanation.walkthrough: Mark Antony's funeral speech in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar opens 'Friends, Romans, ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: Countrymen are people who live in rural areas, i.e. rustic types.
